evidence.fact: Over the past decade, global venture investment in Artificial Intelligence grew over thirty-fold from $8.3 billion to $259 billion.

OpenAI received more than 400 responses to its policy submission window for its 'Industrial Policy for the Intelligence Age' framework ending in June 2026, offering pilot research grants up to $100,000 and up to $1 million in API credits.
On January 14, 2026, the U.S. administration imposed a 25% tariff on a limited set of advanced AI chips imported into the U.S. following a Section 232 investigation.

The U.S. Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) issued a final rule in January 2026 changing license review policies for NVIDIA H200 and AMD MI325X-equivalent chip exports from 'presumption of denial' to case-by-case review.

Draft export control regulations reported in March 2026 outlined a tiered threshold where exports of up to 1,000 Nvidia GB300 GPUs undergo simplified review, while cluster builds exceeding 200,000 units require host-country matching investments in American AI.
evidence.source: Global Trade & Sanctions Law / Industry Reporting

evidence.fact: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) disclosed lobbying expenditures totaling over $2 million in recent quarters regarding the Chip Security Act, AI diffusion policy, and export control rule changes.

KLA Corp. disclosed more than $1 million in lobbying expenditures over a one-year window focusing specifically on trade policy regarding China, tariffs, and export controls on advanced semiconductor manufacturing equipment.
U.S. productivity growth averaged 1.4% over the contemporary tech expansion phase, trailing the historical 2.2% post-World War II average despite multi-billion-dollar scale-ups in AI investments.
